chapter_theme: The nine fire-pits (navakundam) of the fire rite, each of its own shape, read at once as altars and as places in the body: the flame rising in them is the Lord's light, in which Siva, Shakti and Skanda are visualized in forms of fixed numbers. Those who see that fire within are freed from strong karma, live long in the guarded body and reach release.
structure_note: An announcement (1015) is followed by the kundas and the light rising in them (1016 to 1020), the forms seen in the flame, of Shakti, Siva and Skanda (1021 to 1033), and the fruit of joining the fire: release, long life, the guru's teaching and the yogi's inner practice (1034 to 1044). Much of the chapter is technical and some lines look corrupt.

1015.reading: I will tell what the nine kundas are, the good flame that rises in them and all the good that rises in them.
1015.nuance: குண்டம் is the pit for the sacred fire; nine kundas of different shapes belong to the Agamic fire rite. The chapter treats them also as places within, so a plain and an inner reading stand throughout.

1016.reading: Within the kunda spoken of are three parts, the four-cornered pit, five good things and the hostile triple city with fire; the parts that rise beyond these we do not know.
1016.nuance: முக்கால் (three legs, three times or three parts), நாற்கோணம் (square) and பாரங்கி (perhaps earth and fire) are unclear. முப்புரம், the three cities Siva burned, are traditionally read as the three malas. The last line may be corrupt.

1017.reading: That which, thrown upward, made space within, the red flame that knew the breath and entered thought within, which knew the earth and stood with the cosmos unbounded: I knew it and sought it within.
1017.nuance: கால் is taken as breath, as elsewhere in Tirumular, and the red flame as the inner fire. சிறகற (without wings or edges) is obscure.

1018.reading: As the light rising within this kunda one can create and destroy the fourteen worlds; all the spread of the ancient Veda I have set out today as a spoken text.
1018.nuance: The subject of ஆக்கி அழிக்கலாம் is open: the light itself, the Lord, creates and destroys, or the one who knows it gains that power. Line 4 claims this teaching restates the Veda.

1019.reading: In the sixteen places of that kunda the kalas set there stand guarding; for those who see the fire rising within, strong karma, however it boils up, cannot join them.
1019.nuance: பதினாறு கலை are traditionally the sixteen digits, as of the moon. உள்ளெழ (rising within) is what turns the rite inward.

1020.reading: In the kunda rising within the triple peak, the five that dance stand within and without, and the twelve signs of the zodiac rise there; for those who seek it, it is the good flame.
1020.nuance: கூடம் முக்கூடம் (peak, three peaks) and ஆடிய ஐந்து (the five that dance: elements, senses or the five acts) are not fixed by the verse. The twelve signs may be the twelve-part breath or a diagram.

1021.reading: The good flame forms the circle of head and face, flames are the hands held in thought, the body is flame and the linga stands unshaken; she rises as the good flame and is the Good.
1021.nuance: This begins the visualization of a deity's form in the fire. நல்லதென்றாள் is read as 'she who is called the Good', the goddess, which 1022 takes up.

1022.reading: She who is called the Good is the sovereign who has come to us; she who is called the Word, is she the flame-crowned head or the feet? Those who do not ask her who stands gently think her stone, even though they have learned.
1022.nuance: The last line (கல்லதென் றாளையும் கற்றும் வின் வாளே) is unclear and may be corrupt; read here as the learned taking the goddess for stone, the image only.

1023.reading: In the kunda shaped like the young crescent of the sky, two flaming serpents point to the directions, many serpents spread, and the supreme flame took its place within my body.
1023.nuance: விளம்பிறை names the crescent-shaped kunda, one of the nine shapes. The serpents (நாகம்) may be ornaments of the form or the coiled power; பன்னாலு (fourteen, or many fours) is unclear.

1024.reading: The feet that took their place are a single beautiful flame, the feet are those that took up the dance, two hands and six flourish in ease, and the red flame of the face belongs to the three-eyed Lord.
1024.nuance: A form of Siva in the fire, given by parts. நண்ணீர் அதற்கு (approach it) and கையிரண்டு ஆறும் (two hands and six, or two and the six) are unclear.

1025.reading: The three-eyed one is himself the whole flame; that one swallowed all the world; with eyes in every direction he saw the eight quarters; to every god of whatever eyes he is our father and Lord.
1025.nuance: The verse plays on கணன் (the eyed one): முக்கணன், அக்கணன், திக்கணன், எக்கணன். 'Swallowing the world' is usually said of Vishnu; here it is Siva's, and எக்கணன் may glance at the many-eyed gods, Brahma and Indra.

1026.reading: For our father the Lord there are six circles, and because the six-faced one appears before his father and Lord Skanda stays joined there, hold him fast as the son.
1026.nuance: The six-sided kunda is matched with six-faced Murugan. மாட்டிக்கொள்ளீரே (fix, hold fast) is read as a command to the meditator.

1027.reading: In the Veda rising within the kunda, one foot moving and two unfolding, two bent hands and one rising trembling: these gods set there are good light.
1027.nuance: The verse lists limbs of forms seen in the fire, but whose forms and how they are counted is not clear.

1028.reading: As good light she moves through all the world, as the light of a gem she stays mingled within, as the light of the word she follows all lives, and as the gem's light she stands in the eye.
1028.nuance: கல்லொளி (light of stone, a gem's light) is repeated; it may be the inner light seen in meditation. The feminine நின்றாளே makes the subject Shakti.

1029.reading: This kunda does not stay fixed but becomes angled; in the ancient circle the six sixes rise, and as these tattvas mingle within it can be raised, like a heart of space.
1029.nuance: மாறாறும் is read as ஆறாறு, the thirty-six tattvas. விண்ணுளம் (sky-heart, or 'as if the heart of the sky') and the last line are obscure.

1030.reading: Three lifting feet, the letter, two fierce faces with six eyes, a tongue that reads and counts, four horns, and eyes rising close by: these belong to the one without end.
1030.nuance: Another numbered form. கொம்பு and தந்தம் can mean horn or tusk, which might suggest an elephant form, but தந்தமிலாற்கே is read with 1031 as அந்தம் இலாற்கு, the endless one.

1031.reading: The endless one has no place wide enough, no one to measure him and no word to reach him; know the endless one through devotion.
1031.nuance: பத்தே may be devotion (பத்தி) or the number ten, which 1032 opens with. Lines 1 to 3 are the chapter's clearest statement that no form contains the Lord the other verses describe.

1032.reading: In the kunda measured out with ten, eight, six and four, the lotus blooms; bound there it stands as the mingled truth, and settled on Parvati's side.
1032.nuance: The petal counts may be those of lotus centres in the body or of the kunda's drawing. மெய் may be truth or body.

1033.reading: Parvati's partner has twenty hands spread, ten feet, ten faces with their eyes, two flower feet, a flaming crown, forty ears and a good twenty-five.
1033.nuance: The counts do not cohere as given: ten feet (காற்பதி பத்து) then two feet. சோத்திரம் may be ears (srotra) or hymns (stotra); இருபத்தஞ்சு may be the twenty-five tattvas.

1034.reading: The form of five measures five fives; because the kunda blooms there, the supreme flame spreads as light, and to join the cooing fire is release.
1034.nuance: ஐஐந்து (twenty-five) may be the tattvas. மஞ்சிட்ட (cloud-laid) and பஞ்சிட்ட (cotton-laid, or five-laid) are obscure. வன்னி, fire, is named as what one joins for release.

1035.reading: He who is the whole flame, the good light of release, abides in the thought of those who stand beyond learning; those who seek without attachment, pass through the spreading light and are free of hostility have joined him.
1035.nuance: கற்றற்று is read as 'with learning ended' but may hide another word; செற்றற்து in line 4 is taken as செற்றற்று, 'without enmity'.

1036.reading: The five kalas joined, this kunda and all the directions settle there; those who have kindled the fire that the five elements watch are ever joined with it.
1036.nuance: The five kalas are traditionally nivritti, pratishtha, vidya, shanti and shantyatita. காய்ந்தவர் may be those who kindled or heated the fire, or those who overcame it.

1037.reading: Join the One who made the seven worlds of the wide waters a region of truth and of rescue; the gods made perfect by knowledge seen in practice have mingled with the reality that has no false part.
1037.nuance: The verse plays on கண்டம் (region, part): மெய்கண்டம், உய்கண்டம், செய்கண்ட, பொய்கண்டம்.

1038.reading: The two feet joined become two hands, the kunda opens at the syllable ma as the nose, the red face blooms with the other eye and forehead, and the tuft of hair is there for the Supreme.
1038.nuance: Line 2 is corrupt (a stray Latin Y). The verse seems to map a form, and perhaps mantra syllables, onto the kunda, but the mapping cannot be fixed.

1039.reading: The Supreme's light is there as a child on one side, blooms as one in the middle, spreads to the west and hollows, and flourishes as the creeper, Shakti.
1039.nuance: பாலன், மத்திமன் (child, middle one) may be stages of the Lord's form or positions. பச்சிம திக்கு, the west, in yogic usage can mean the back channel. கொடி (creeper) is a common image for Shakti.

1040.reading: The kunda where the creeper ran its six courses and played is two-angled at the base and alike at the end; those who see unfailingly the flame spread through the seven worlds become a great treasure.
1040.nuance: கொடியாறு (six courses of the creeper, or the creeper's river) may be the six centres of the body. மாதனம் (great wealth) is taken up in 1041.

1041.reading: Taking as his means the fire that grows as great wealth, the guru stands perfected and teaches it fittingly, and the feet that rule the world, seeing it, are moved with love.
1041.nuance: The verse rhymes on -தனம்: மாதனம், சாதனம், போதனம், பாதனம். Who sees and is moved in the last line, the Lord or the guru, is not certain.

1042.reading: No one examines and knows as their own the light that spreads wherever one looks; those who guarded the body and dwelt in thought within it have grown old in that body and seen a crore of ages.
1042.nuance: ஆத்தம் (one's own, or trustworthy) is unclear. The claim of long life in the guarded body is plain and fits Tirumular's teaching of nurturing the body.

1043.reading: The nine kundas known over the ages are alike; the yogi who has seen within raises them in the nadi, and as the womb conceives on union, seeing the world through this is the practice.
1043.nuance: The verse makes the nine kundas inner and raised through the channels. The third line (பகங்கண்டு கொண்டஇப் பாய்கரு) is read as an image of conception; சகம் கண்டு may be seeing or creating the world.

1044.reading: Four practices, three fires, the bilva, the circle of pain, six that grow, the flower-stage, teaching, five flowers, the false elephant: seeking the Lord in these is nine crore.
1044.nuance: The verse is a compressed list whose items cannot be fixed; தழல் மூன்று are traditionally the three sacred fires. நவகோடி may be nine crore or nine kinds. Some words may be corrupt.

links.note: 1030 and the verses around it give the Lord counted feet, faces and eyes in the fire; 1031 says the endless one has no place, no measure and no word that reaches him. The forms are aids, not limits.
724 says Tirumular learned to nurture the body so as to nurture life; 1042 says those who guarded the body and dwelt within it lived through a crore of ages.
Both say deeds cannot cling to the one turned to the Lord: the Kural through his true praise, Tirumular through seeing the fire rise within.

1015 announces the நவகுண்டம், the nine fire-pits, and the good that rises in them. 360, in the story of Daksha's sacrifice, names the same நவகுண்டம் ஒன்பதும், which the gods ask Siva to make a source of joy for the good. The term that the chapter turns inward into places of the body appears in 360 as the outward sacrificial altar.

1016 lists among the kunda's parts பகைத்திடு முப்புரம், the hostile triple city, with fire. 343 says fools take it literally that Siva burned the three cities, and that முப்புரம் is the work of the three impurities (மும்மல காரியம்). 343 supplies the reading by which the triple city in 1016's fire-pit is the soul's malas being burned.

1017 speaks of a செஞ்சுடர், red flame, that knew the breath (கால் அறிந்து) and entered thought within. 1777 has the practitioner pass through the rising செஞ்சுடர் while the breath (ஆவி) rises as far as the body allows, and says holding this is the supreme state. Both place the red flame and the breath together as the inner fire of yoga.

1018 ends: the whole spread of the ancient Veda (பண்டையுள் வேதம்) I have set out today as a spoken text (இன்றுசொல் நூலாய்). In 81 Tirumular says the Lord made him well so that he would render the Lord well in Tamil (தமிழ்செய்யுமாறே). Together they show the poet's view of his own book: a new telling, in Tamil, of what was already revealed.

1021 sees a form rising as நற்சுடர், the good flame, and names her நல்லது என்றாள், the goddess. 1091 sees the young creeper, Shakti, within ஓமப் பெருஞ்சுடர், the great flame of the fire rite, and the fine smoke rising in it. Both make the flame of the homa the place where Shakti is seen.

1022 says those who do not ask her who stands gently take her for stone, even though they have learned (கற்றும்); the last line is unclear and may be corrupt. 318 calls those who have learned yet lack Siva-knowledge (கற்றும் சிவஞானம் இல்லா) wretches and fools. On the reading of 1022 given, both say learning without inner knowing leaves one blind to what is holy.

1023 ends: the supreme flame (பரஞ்சுடர்) took its place within my body (என் ஆகத்துள்ளே இடங்கொண்டவாறே). 2324 says the flawless Shakti, the light of a great gem, was seen within the flesh (ஊனிடைக் கண்டதே). Both locate the supreme light in the speaker's own body, 1023 through the image of the fire-pit.

1025 calls the three-eyed one (முக்கணன்) the whole flame (முழுச்சுடர்), the one who swallowed all and saw the eight directions. 2684 explains the three eyes: sun and moon are his eyes and fire is the other eye in his forehead, making his body one of light. 2684 spells out why the three-eyed one of 1025 is himself the flame.

1026 says the six-faced one appears before his father (தந்தைதன் முன்னே சண்முகம் தோன்றலால்) and tells the meditator to hold him as the son (மைந்தன்). Thiruppugazh 602 names Murugan as the one who taught his father, who keeps Shakti at his side, the whole truth of the Veda (மறைநூலின் தத்துவ தற்பரம் முற்றும் உணர்த்திய). Tirumular places Skanda in the father's fire as the son; Arunagiri makes the son the father's teacher.

1031 says the endless one has no place wide enough, no one to measure him and no word that reaches him, and is known only by devotion (பத்தே). 448 says he is vast (அகன்றான்), the seven wide worlds one in him, and not easy to point to as 'this is he' (இவன்தான் என... எளியனும் அல்லன்). Both deny that the Lord can be measured or pointed out, and 1031 adds devotion as the way to know him.

1032 has the measured kunda (மட்டிட்ட குண்டம்) bloom as a lotus that stands bound (கட்டிட்டு நின்று). 662 uses the same words: in the stalk of the bound lotus (கட்டிட்ட தாமரை) the adorned maidens (மட்டிட்ட கன்னியர்) joined the Lady, standing bound (கட்டிட்டு நின்று). The shared wording shows the kunda's lotus is the same inner lotus of the yogic body.

1033 gives Parvati's partner by counts: twenty hands, ten faces with eyes, two flower feet and a flaming crown. 1730 gives Sadasiva the same way: two feet together on the pedestal, arms two and eight, five faces. Both describe a form of Siva by numbered limbs, and the counts differ, so the numbers belong to particular forms rather than one fixed image.

1034 says that to join the fire (வன்னியைக் கூடுதல்) is release. 2987 says those who can perform a thousand fire offerings (ஓமம் ஓர் ஆயிரம்) have seen through a thousand desires and are done with them. 2987 credits the outer homa with ending desire; 1034 goes further and makes union with the fire itself mukti.

1035 says those who seek without attachment (பற்றற நாடி) and pass through the spreading light have joined the one who is the whole flame. Kural 350 says to cling to the one without clinging (பற்றற்றான் பற்றினை) in order to let clinging go. Both make the end of attachment the condition for reaching the Lord, and Tirumular's பற்றற echoes the Kural's paradox.

1038, mapping a form onto the kunda, has the red face bloom with மற்றைக்கண் நெற்றி, the other eye in the forehead. 2684 uses the same phrase: fire is மற்றைக்கண் நெற்றி, the third eye, beside the sun and moon. The shared words show the forehead eye in the kunda form is the fire-eye of the Lord's body of light.

1039 ends with the Lord's light flourishing as Shakti, சத்திமானாகத் தழைத்த கொடி, the creeper. 2445 has the young creeper (இளங்கொடி) hang down and do good after the speaker reaches the First of the three-tiered circle within. In both the creeper is Shakti growing within, as the light of the Lord the speaker has reached.

1041 rhymes on மாதனம் and சாதனம்: the fire growing as great wealth, and the guru perfected with it as his means. 721 tells the reader to worship the guru who is the means (சாதனமாகும் குருவை) and value him as great wealth (மாதனமாக). The same two words make the guru both the means and the treasure in both verses.

1042 says those who guarded the body (காத்துடல்) and dwelt within it in thought grew old in it and saw a crore of ages (மூத்துடல் கோடி யுகம்). 758 says those who reached the hundred guard the body (காத்துடல்) and live into a crore of yugas (மூத்துடன் கோடி யுகம்). The near-repeat restates Tirumular's claim of long life in the guarded body.

1043 says the nine kundas are alike and the yogi who has seen within raises them in the நாடி. 658 places in the nine-gated body one place with nine channels (ஒன்பது நாடி), and says those who can still them gain visions. 1043 maps the nine fire-pits onto that inner set of nine, making the rite a matter of the channels.

source_issues: 1038 line 2 (மலர்ந்திரு குண்ட மகாரத்தார் Yமூக்கு) contains a stray Latin 'Y' and is corrupt.
1035 line 4: செற்றற்து is probably a misprint for செற்றற்று.
1022 line 4: கற்றும் வின் வாளே is split oddly and unclear; perhaps வினவாரே or a corruption.
1033: the numbers do not cohere (ten feet in line 2, two feet in line 3).
1016 line 4 and 1044 lines 2 to 3 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1030 line 4: தந்தமி லாற்கே is read as அந்தம் இலாற்கு (to the endless one), matching 1031; the division of words is uncertain.
